source.title: Middle-Layer Representation Alignment for Cross-Lingual Transfer in Fine-Tuned LLMs

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-lingual representation retrieval, finds weak and layer-dependent baseline alignment, and tests how alignment changes with training objectives and alignment-data choices. This refines the claim toward condition-dependent rather than general convergence.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own translation-retrieval measurements of representation alignment. Downstream task scores and transfer improvements are not rows because they measure task performance, not representational alignment. The paper discusses cosine and SVCCA as alternatives but does not report a comparison of those metrics.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-lingual alignment inside a single LLM: whether mean-pooled activations for translations of the same sentence retrieve each other. It does not compare representations across independently trained models, modalities, seeds or SAE features, and does not test metric dependence of cross-model convergence. Most retrieval gains come from a contrastive objective built to produce alignment, which induces the effect on purpose. No row measures what any version names, so this is a related construct, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' emphasis is practical: middle-layer alignment during fine-tuning improves cross-lingual task transfer, especially for low-resource languages. They also find it robust to the choice of alignment languages and domain, and that alignment modules can be merged post hoc. The record's 'results depend on data domain' overstates the authors' view; they say same-domain data is not strictly necessary.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures translation-retrieval accuracy from mean-pooled layer activations and trains a contrastive alignment objective on parallel sentences. It does not perform a model-size or capability sweep or compare independently trained cross-modal models.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval varies by layer; low-resource languages have weaker alignment; single-language alignment trails multilingual alignment; FLoRes, Tatoeba, and IWSLT alignment data produce different retrieval results.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single LLM (Llama 3 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B), translations' mean-pooled representations retrieve each other at under 50% on average over 1,190 pairs. Retrieval peaks at middle layers and is much weaker for low-resource languages. Task fine-tuning leaves it unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within multilingual LLMs, representations of semantically equivalent text in different languages partially converge, most strongly in middle layers (cross-lingual semantic hub).

fits_no_version.finding: A middle-layer contrastive objective raises within-model cross-lingual retrieval (Llama 39.4 to 73.2), but not for Qwen on slot-filling languages (20.9 to 20.5). The gain depends on loss placement, alignment-language diversity and data domain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit contrastive training can induce cross-lingual representational alignment in LLMs, with effects depending on layer, language coverage and domain.

record.problems: Only two LLM families are analyzed; no model-scale or independent-seed comparison is conducted. Main layerwise results are presented in figures without exact values, and the paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the retrieval accuracies. Machine-translation retrieval partly overlaps its training data, which the authors note may inflate those scores.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Downstream task-performance results were left out because they measure task outcomes rather than representation alignment.

untested.parts: No comparison across independently trained models and no scale sweep.
No vision-language models or image-caption pairs.
No cross-model mapping or stitching. LoRA module merging is weight averaging within one model, not representation mapping.
No cross-model convergence measure whose metric or input dependence is tested. Retrieval is chosen over cosine and SVCCA without a comparison.
No cross-model alignment, plateau, or shared-data explanation tested.

record.verdict_notes: The study does not concern convergence between different models, so it gives no verdicts. Corrections to the extracted Table 2 values: the MT retrieval column is the bracketed one (Llama 51.5/55.3/84.5, Qwen 36.5/38.8/75.6), not 15.5/17.0 and 14.6/14.7, which are BLEU. Base-model (no-SFT) retrieval for the slot-filling languages is 39.1 for Llama and 21.4 for Qwen. The model used in the Table 6 ablations is unspecified.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of independent models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities converging as they scale.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language models.
No comparison of independently initialized seeds or shared features/subspaces across seeds.
No test of mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability between models.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

The study varies layer, alignment-language selection, and alignment-data domain, but does not compare retrieval with cosine, SVCCA, or other similarity measures, nor test out-of-distribution retrieval inputs.

The study reports weak or incomplete retrieval alignment and manipulates alignment training data/objectives, but does not test a plateau with scale or compare shared pretraining data/objectives against a common model of reality across independent models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Retrieval varies with layer placement and with the alignment languages/domain; middle-layer alignment has broader effects, while single-language or different-domain settings yield lower results (r13-r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study uses retrieval accuracy and discusses cosine/SVCCA but does not compare metrics, and it does not test out-of-distribution retrieval inputs (r1-r4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Alignment trained with selected multilingual data/objectives
reader_labels.reason: Adding an explicit alignment objective raises Llama's retrieval accuracy substantially; multilingual alignment data also score above the single-pair settings (r9, r16-r19).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors report weak baseline alignment, and the alignment objective does not improve Qwen retrieval in slot filling; gains in other reported retrieval settings are incomplete (r1-r4, r10-r12).
